phases.title: Positioning and Layering
phases.description: Take boxes out of normal flow, anchor overlays, and control which layer paints on top.

questions.prompt: Why does an absolutely positioned element stop reserving space in the layout?
questions.fullGoal: Explain absolute positioning and normal flow.
questions.expectedAnswer: Absolute positioning removes the box from normal flow and positions it against the nearest positioned ancestor, so its original space collapses.
questions.rubric: Check removal from flow and the containing block.

questions.prompt: Name two reasons a position: sticky element might fail to stick.
questions.expectedAnswer: It needs an offset such as top: 0, and an ancestor with overflow hidden or auto, a transform, or a filter can break it; it also stops at the edge of its parent.
questions.rubric: Check the offset and at least one ancestor or parent constraint.

questions.prompt: What creates a stacking context, and why does that matter for z-index?
questions.expectedAnswer: A positioned element with a z-index, opacity below 1, a transform, filter, or isolation can create a stacking context; z-index only competes inside its context, so a high value cannot escape.
questions.rubric: Check a stacking-context trigger and the containment effect.

questions.prompt: Why is the native dialog element a better base for a modal than a positioned div?
questions.expectedAnswer: It provides modal semantics, focus handling, Escape to close, and a backdrop, while a div requires those behaviors to be rebuilt and tested.
questions.rubric: Check semantics, focus, and dismissal.

questions.prompt: Why should a design use a small set of z-index tokens instead of 9999?
questions.expectedAnswer: Tokens keep layer order intentional and predictable; arbitrary large values start an arms race and still cannot escape a parent stacking context.
questions.rubric: Check predictable order and the stacking-context limit.

questions.prompt: Make .site-header stick to the top of the viewport and sit above ordinary page content.
questions.fullGoal: Use sticky positioning with an offset and a z-index.
questions.expectedAnswer: .site-header { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10; }
questions.rubric: Check sticky positioning, the top offset, and a sensible z-index.

phases.title: Motion and Visual Effects
phases.description: Animate state changes with transitions and keyframes, use transforms and filters, and respect a motion budget.

questions.prompt: Why should a transition be declared on the base rule instead of only on :hover?
questions.expectedAnswer: The base rule animates both entering and leaving the state; a transition only on hover animates one direction and snaps back.
questions.rubric: Check both directions of the state change.

questions.prompt: Why are transform and opacity better animation properties than width and top?
questions.expectedAnswer: Transform and opacity can be composited without layout or paint, while width and top trigger layout on each frame and can drop frames.
questions.rubric: Check layout and paint cost.

questions.prompt: What should happen to animation when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce?
questions.expectedAnswer: Remove or replace non-essential motion, such as disabling transitions and looping animations while keeping content and state changes usable.
questions.rubric: Check respect for the user preference.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between opacity and an alpha color?
questions.expectedAnswer: Opacity fades the whole element including its text and children, while an alpha color fades only that paint layer and lets the background show through.
questions.rubric: Check whole-element versus single-layer transparency.

questions.prompt: When several background layers are declared, which one paints on top?
questions.expectedAnswer: The layer listed first in the background shorthand or background-image list paints on top, with later layers behind it.
questions.rubric: Check first-listed on top.

questions.prompt: Make .card fade to 60% opacity on hover with a 150ms transition.
questions.fullGoal: Use a transition and a hover state.
questions.expectedAnswer: .card { transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .card:hover { opacity: 0.6; }
questions.rubric: Check the base transition, the hover selector, and the opacity value.

phases.title: Components and Content
phases.description: Style the parts people actually use: links, navigation, forms, tables, icons, and generated content.

questions.prompt: Why is a visible label better than a placeholder for a form field?
questions.expectedAnswer: A label stays visible after typing, gives the control a reliable accessible name, and can carry a stronger contrast than placeholder text.
questions.rubric: Check persistence and accessible naming.

questions.prompt: How do you make a data table adapt to a narrow screen without destroying its semantics?
questions.expectedAnswer: Wrap the table in a horizontally scrollable container with keyboard access and an accessible name, and keep the table, caption, and header cells intact.
questions.rubric: Check scrolling wrapper and preserved table semantics.

questions.prompt: What is required for ::before and ::after to appear, and what should they not be used for?
questions.expectedAnswer: They need the content property. They should not carry essential text or interactive controls because they are not part of the DOM and cannot receive events or focus.
questions.rubric: Check content and the essential-content restriction.

questions.prompt: How do CSS counters number a list of steps?
questions.expectedAnswer: Reset the counter on the container, increment it on each item, and display it with content: counter(name), usually in a pseudo-element.
questions.rubric: Check reset, increment, and display.

questions.prompt: Why use :user-invalid instead of :invalid for a required field?
questions.expectedAnswer: An empty required field matches :invalid immediately, while :user-invalid waits until the user has interacted, so the page does not start in an error state.
questions.rubric: Check pre-interaction behavior.

questions.prompt: Give an input inside .field a visible keyboard focus ring with a 2px solid #2563eb outline.
questions.fullGoal: Style keyboard focus on a form control.
questions.expectedAnswer: .field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; }
questions.rubric: Check the descendant selector, focus-visible, and the outline.

phases.title: Modern CSS and Architecture
phases.description: Keep styles maintainable with native nesting, cascade layers, feature queries, relational selectors, logical properties, and themes.

questions.prompt: What is one difference between native CSS nesting and a preprocessor such as Sass?
questions.expectedAnswer: Native nesting runs in the browser without a build step and uses & for the parent, but it does not support string concatenation such as &__title.
questions.rubric: Check browser execution and one accurate limitation.

questions.prompt: Where do unlayered normal declarations sit relative to cascade layers?
questions.expectedAnswer: Unlayered normal declarations win over layered normal declarations, while important declarations reverse the layer order and unlayered important declarations lose.
questions.rubric: Check normal unlayered priority and the important reversal.

questions.prompt: What does @supports test, and what does it not guarantee?
questions.expectedAnswer: It tests whether the browser can parse a declaration or selector; it does not guarantee that the feature works correctly or looks right.
questions.rubric: Check syntax detection and the lack of behavior testing.

questions.prompt: What does :has() let you style, and give one practical example.
questions.expectedAnswer: It styles an element based on whether a relative selector matches inside it, such as styling a field wrapper when its input is user-invalid.
questions.rubric: Check relational matching and a concrete use.

questions.prompt: What does @property add to a custom property?
questions.expectedAnswer: It registers a syntax type, an inheritance rule, and an initial value, which enables validation and interpolation.
questions.rubric: Check type, inheritance, initial value, or animation.

questions.prompt: Give .card 16px of padding on the inline axis and 24px on the block axis using logical properties.
questions.expectedAnswer: .card { padding-inline: 16px; padding-block: 24px; }
questions.rubric: Check padding-inline and padding-block with the correct values.
